reasons.plausibility: The mechanism of oxide film passivation at low temperature and its degradation at higher temperature is well-founded in corrosion science for steel, making this hypothesis credible.
reasons.testability: The proposed design with precisely controlled oxide removal and clear comparative analyses between treated and untreated samples at two temperatures offers a direct, definitive test of the hypothesis.
reasons.usefulness: It provides a targeted experimental strategy to clarify the protective role of the native oxide on Q235 steel and how it changes with temperature, which can inform practical corrosion mitigation measures.
